name: IN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Yakym has a massive fundraising advantage ($5.2M vs $0.4M)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only ~4%
No polls or expert ratings to suggest competitive dynamics
model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean, Yakym's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing Democratic odds near 4% all point the same direction, justifying a margin slightly beyond the fundamentals-only estimate. With no polls or ratings indicating vulnerability, this sits firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing Yakym under 55% against Decio, or major outside spending entering the district, would warrant a downgrade toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North-central Indiana's second district is solidly Republican territory, and incumbent Rudy Yakym is seeking a full term after winning the seat in 2022. He has raised over $5 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Jamee Decio, who has raised about $356,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets give Democrats only about a 4% chance. The district's strong Republican lean and the incumbent's financial dominance make an upset highly unlikely, and the forecast treats this as safely Republican with modest residual uncertainty from the absence of polling.
